outcome: The problem itself (the exact asymptotic value of lim M(n)/n) remains open, but the upper bound has been repeatedly improved by a sequence of AI systems since mid-2025: AlphaEvolve (0.380924, mid-2025), TogetherAI's EinsteinArena agents (0.380871, early 2026), TTT-Discover (0.380876, reported before TogetherAI's improvement in the same window), and SimpleTES (0.380868, April 2026) — each beating the prior record, all beating the pre-2024 best human bound of 0.380926/0.380927 due to Haugland (2016). The lower bound (0.379005, White 2022) has not moved in the window.

ai.basis_quote: AlphaEvolve established a new upper bound for the minimum overlap problem, slightly improving upon the previous record. Each generation of AlphaEvolve was tasked with evolving a program representing a search heuristic... TTT-Discover improved the upper bound on Erdős' Minimum Overlap Problem to 0.380876, surpassing AlphaEvolve's recent construction with 0.380924... the solution from TTT-Discover is an asymmetric construction, finding a 600-piece step function... 'It is straightforward to verify that the provided functions give bounds that improve upon the state of the art' (Prof. Davide Torlo, expert reviewer). SimpleTES reaches 0.380868, ahead of the best human (0.380927), AlphaEvolve (0.380924, Gemini-2.0 Pro), and TogetherAI (0.380871).

disputes.summary: Four separate AI systems from different groups (Google DeepMind's AlphaEvolve, Together AI's EinsteinArena agents, Yuksekgonul et al.'s TTT-Discover, and Ye et al.'s SimpleTES) each claimed a new record upper bound within roughly a nine-month window (June 2025 to April 2026), each explicitly framed as beating the immediately preceding AI record. The exact chronological order between TTT-Discover's 0.380876 and TogetherAI's 0.380871 was not fully pinned down from primary timestamps; the current Wikipedia article and SimpleTES blog post both treat SimpleTES's 0.380868 as the most recent and tightest.

summary: This is a bound-type bullet (asymptotic constant c = lim M(n)/n for Erdős's 1955 minimum overlap problem), so under §3.1 a bound moving counts directly, and it moved several times. Before the frozen revision the state was: lower bound 0.379005 (White, arXiv 2201.05704, Jan 2022) and upper bound 0.380926 (Haugland 2016, 'The minimum overlap problem revisited', arXiv 1609.08000) — both pre-2024 and unchanged in the window as far as the lower bound goes. Starting mid-2025 a chain of AI systems repeatedly tightened the upper bound: Google DeepMind's AlphaEvolve (Novikov et al., arXiv 2506.13131, submitted 16 June 2025) evolved a search-heuristic program that discovered a 95-piece step-function construction giving upper bound 0.380924, the first upper-bound improvement since 2016; the paper's own account (quoted in ai.basis_quote) describes AlphaEvolve evolving the search heuristic itself, with the paper's acknowledgements crediting mathematicians Javier Gomez Serrano and Terence Tao only with suggesting/formulating the problem, not with producing the construction — so this is `generated`, not merely `assisted`. Subsequently, Together AI's EinsteinArena agents produced 0.380871 (repository last updated 1 April 2026, 'purely obtained by AI agents'); Yuksekgonul et al.'s TTT-Discover (arXiv 2601.16175, test-time RL fine-tuning of an LLM) found an asymmetric 600-piece step function giving 0.380876, explicitly reported as surpassing AlphaEvolve's 0.380924 and verified by an outside human expert (Prof. Davide Torlo) who confirmed the bound but did not himself produce it; and Ye et al.'s SimpleTES (arXiv 2604.19341, using only the open-source gpt-oss-120b/20b models) reached 0.380868, described on the authors' own blog as ahead of the best human (0.380927), AlphaEvolve (0.380924), and TogetherAI (0.380871). All of these are upper-bound improvements on a problem that remains fully open (no exact value of the constant is known), so status is `progress` rather than `resolved`/`claimed`/`partial` — nothing was proved to be exactly true or false, a number simply moved, repeatedly. I used the earliest well-documented event (AlphaEvolve, June 2025) as the anchor `event` since it is the first AI-driven change from the pre-2024 baseline; the later improvements (TogetherAI, TTT-Discover, SimpleTES) are described in this summary rather than given separate records, per the instruction to keep one decisive event per record. `resolution_direction` is null because `progress` never takes a direction. `ai_role` is `generated` for all four systems on the authors' own accounts: in each case the construction itself (the step function achieving the bound) was produced by the AI system, with humans only verifying it, suggesting the problem, or running verification notebooks — none of the sources describe a human producing part of the mathematical content that ended up in the winning construction.
competing_reading: One could argue AlphaEvolve's role is closer to `assisted` since it 'evolved a search heuristic' rather than directly outputting the final numeric construction, and since named mathematicians (Gomez Serrano, Tao) were involved in problem formulation. But the paper is explicit that the program AlphaEvolve evolved is what searched for and found the improved construction — the humans' contribution was posing/formalizing the problem, not producing part of the mathematics in the result, which under §6.2 keeps this at `generated` rather than `assisted`. Also arguable: since four different AI systems each improved on the last with no single 'the' event, one could treat this as `open` with a `bound` role for the whole sequence rather than `progress`/`generated`; I judged AlphaEvolve's initial jump (first improvement since 2016) as the anchor `generated` event because it produced the qualifying construction itself, with `ai_role` describing that first and clearest case, and the subsequent chain narrated in `summary`.
what_would_settle_it: A primary-source timestamp resolving the exact order of the TTT-Discover (0.380876) and TogetherAI (0.380871) results relative to each other, and confirmation of whether any newer AI or human result has superseded SimpleTES's 0.380868 since April 2026.
